cards.claim: Patch-whitening initialization on the first convolutional layer dramatically accelerates CIFAR-10 training to 94% accuracy
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 1.97M parameter VGG-like CNN, batch size 1024, Nesterov SGD, single A100 GPU
cards.effect: Reduces epochs from 45 to 21 and time from 18.3 to 8.0 A100-seconds for 94% accuracy (>2x speedup)
cards.evidence: Direct experimental measurement comparing baseline with and without patch-whitening initialization
cards.quote: Patch-whitening initialization is the single most impactful feature. Adding it to the baseline more than doubles training speed so that we reach 94% accuracy in 21 epochs taking 8.0 A100-seconds.

cards.claim: Identity initialization of post-first convolution layers as partial identity transforms improves CIFAR-10 training speed
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 1.97M parameter VGG-like CNN, built on patched-whitening baseline, batch size 1024, Nesterov SGD
cards.effect: Reduces epochs from 21 to 18 and time from 8.0 to 6.8 A100-seconds for 94% accuracy
cards.evidence: Direct experimental measurement of adding identity initialization feature (dirac_) to baseline
cards.quote: With this feature added, training attains 94% accuracy in 18 epochs taking 6.8 A100-seconds.

cards.claim: Increased learning rate for BatchNorm biases (by factor noted in paper) accelerates CIFAR-10 training
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 1.97M parameter VGG-like CNN, with patch-whitening and identity init, batch size 1024, Nesterov SGD
cards.effect: Reduces epochs from 18 to 13.5 and time from 6.8 to 5.1 A100-seconds for 94% accuracy
cards.evidence: Direct experimental measurement of adding scalebias feature
cards.quote: We increase the learning rate for the learnable biases of all BatchNorm layers by a factor of , following Page (2019) ; tysam-code (2023) . With this feature added, training reaches 94% in 13.5 epochs taking 5.1 A100-seconds.

cards.claim: Lookahead optimizer improves CIFAR-10 training speed for short budgets
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 1.97M parameter VGG-like CNN, with prior optimizations, batch size 1024, <15 epochs
cards.effect: Reduces epochs from 13.5 to 12.0 and time from 5.1 to 4.6 A100-seconds for 94% accuracy
cards.evidence: Direct experimental measurement of adding Lookahead optimization
cards.quote: Following tysam-code (2023) , we use Lookahead ( Zhang et al., 2019 ) optimization. With this feature added, training reaches 94% in 12.0 epochs taking 4.6 A100-seconds.

cards.claim: GELU activation functions are used instead of standard activations in the network architecture
cards.effect: Part of optimized recipe; specific ablation effect not isolated but contributes to overall training acceleration
cards.quote: We use GELU ( Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016 ) activations.

cards.claim: Disabling biases in convolutional and linear layers, and affine parameters in BatchNorm improves training efficiency
cards.effect: Part of optimized baseline configuration; combined effect contributes to reaching 94% in <15 epochs
cards.evidence: Architectural design choice in baseline network
cards.quote: Following Page (2019) ; tysam-code (2023) , we disable the biases of convolutional and linear layers, and disable the affine scale parameters of BatchNorm layers.

cards.claim: Output scaling by factor 1/9 on final linear layer improves CIFAR-10 accuracy
cards.effect: Part of final optimized configuration contributing to 94% accuracy at ~10 epochs
cards.evidence: Architectural design choice in baseline network
cards.quote: The output of the final linear layer is scaled down by a constant factor of 1/9.

cards.claim: Alternating (derandomized) horizontal flip augmentation outperforms standard random flipping for short CIFAR-10 training
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 9.9-40 epochs, single A100 GPU, various configurations with/without Cutout
cards.effect: Effective speedup of 27% at 20 epochs, 38% at 40 epochs without Cutout; maintains 94% accuracy in 9.9 epochs vs. 12+ with random flip
cards.evidence: Systematic experiments across 24 CIFAR-10 configurations comparing alternating vs random flip with power-law fitting of epochs-to-error curves
cards.quote: Adding this feature allows us to shorten training to its final duration of 9.9 epochs, yielding our final training method airbench94.py , the entire contents of which can be found in Section E . It reaches 94% accuracy in 3.83 seconds on an NVIDIA A100.

cards.claim: Reflection padding for 2-pixel translation augmentation is superior to zero-padding
cards.effect: Improves translation augmentation effectiveness relative to zero-padding variant
cards.evidence: Comparative architectural choice in baseline design
cards.quote: For translation we use reflection padding ( Zagoruyko & Komodakis, 2016 ) which we found to be better than zero-padding.

cards.claim: Label smoothing rate of 0.2 is effective for short-budget CIFAR-10 training
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 1.97M parameter VGG-like CNN, Nesterov SGD, batch size 1024
cards.effect: Part of baseline configuration reaching 94% accuracy in 45 epochs; combined with other optimizations enables <15 epoch training
cards.evidence: Explicit hyperparameter choice in baseline training configuration
cards.quote: As our baseline, we train using Nesterov SGD at batch size 1024, with a label smoothing rate of 0.2.

cards.claim: Multi-crop test-time augmentation (6 crops) improves CIFAR-10 test accuracy on short training budgets
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, 10.8 epochs, trained network evaluations, weighted average of 6 augmented views
cards.effect: Reduces effective epochs needed from 12.0 to 10.8 for maintaining 94% accuracy (equivalent speedup)
cards.evidence: Direct experimental measurement of adding multi-crop TTA feature
cards.quote: With this feature added, training reaches 94% in 10.8 epochs taking 4.2 A100-seconds.
